description:
`jit issue reject` leaves a dependent in `backlog` when it removes the dependent's last blocker, so the dependent never becomes available and `jit validate` fails on the repository.

## Background

Reproduced on a fresh repository with the installed binary and with main's build: create a blocker and a dependent, add the edge, run `jit issue reject <blocker> --reason obsolete`, and the dependent stays `backlog`. `Rejected` is a terminal state, so the dependency is met. It surfaced in this repository: rejecting 627fdcc4 left cc6ef886 in `backlog` and 9c008d2d's validation refused the repository.

Closing an issue promotes its dependents through `check_auto_transitions`; `reject_issue` does not reach it. da12ad66 made `jit issue reject` the only rejection form, so this is now the only path.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: After `jit issue reject` removes a dependent's last blocker, the dependent is `ready`, in the same mutation, and `jit validate` passes.
- [hard] REQ-02: Rejection promotes through the same path closing uses, with no second derivation (`@/charter/D-20`).
- [hard] REQ-03: A harness test owns REQ-01.

## Notes

- This must land before the format 3 window: its binary carries 9c008d2d's stricter validation, so every rejection would otherwise break `jit validate` in every repository.
title: Rejecting an issue does not promote its dependents
